mechanism_narrative: The four-week improvement in RETAIL_REC from -66.4 to -57.6, coupled with rising GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT, signals mobility recovery momentum that will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is not higher than mean over last 28 days while RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, and TRANSIT all continue to improve.

mechanism_narrative: The 14.1-point weekly jump in PARKS from -51.4 to -37.3 signals a spring outdoor-activity surge that pulls forward discretionary spending on recreation and retail goods, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 14 days is not higher than mean over last 14 days after a PARKS weekly rise greater than 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improvements are mutually reinforcing: commuting recovery requires both transit use and workplace presence to rise together, and their joint increase will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is less than or equal to mean over last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime where RESIDENTIAL declines week-on-week, residents spend more time outside the home; this behavioral shift will raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL declines, RETAIL_REC mean over next 14 days is not higher than mean over last 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Policy-driven reopening expands transit capacity and store occupancy; as TRANSIT crosses above -55%, it confirms easing restrictions and will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves above -55% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is not higher than mean over last 28 days after TRANSIT exceeds -55% for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week improvement in GROCERY_PHARM from -35.1 to -25.6 indicates reduced stock-up urgency; households shift trips from grocery and pharmacy to discretionary retail, raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 7 days is not higher than mean over last 7 days while GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve.

mechanism_narrative: The PARKS surge above -40% reflects outdoor recreation substitution; indoor retail and recreation footfall falls as residents choose parks over stores, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 7 days is not lower than mean over last 7 days when PARKS is above -40%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL decline and TRANSIT increase jointly signal out-of-home mobility; their interaction raises discretionary retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls and TRANSIT rises in the same week
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL declines and TRANSIT rises in the same week, RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is less than or equal to mean over last 28 days.
